catalog_quote: 4.3.2 Stress. The stress is not an important feature of Bagri, yet, it seems that its existence and phonemic status cannot be ruled out. Stress is utilized in disyllabic syllables to distinguish between grammatical categories. In nouns, stress accent falls on the initial syllable and in the verb category stress accent falls on the final syllable. The stressed syllable is marked by the symbol [ˈ] Nouns: ˈbəlla 'evil spirit', ˈhilla 'job', ˈsilla 'rumour'; Verbs: bəˈlla 'call', hiˈlla 'cause to move', siˈlla 'cause to wet'. Phonetically, stress is employed to express emphasis. The phonetic correlate is the combination of length and pitch. Emphasized syllables contain a greater amount of energy. 4.3.3 Tones / Pitch. Bagri has developed tonal contrasts like Punjabi language. Though it is a very controversial aspect of the suprasegmentals of the Bagri, yet there are known to be three tones. …

audit.reasoning: Quote verified verbatim on the page image of thesis p. 196 (PDF p. 204) and in the djvu text layer; locator correct. The deciding source is the only full grammar of Bagri (Gusain 1999, JNU PhD, 253 pp, supervised by Abbi), which is also the source behind the published Lincom sketch; no dedicated stress/prosody or JIPA-type study of Bagri exists in Glottolog, Crossref, archive.org, Wikipedia's bibliography or Shodhganga. The coding 'morphological' (noun-initial vs verb-final stress in disyllables, stress otherwise marginal, tone prominent) faithfully reflects the source, including its hedge. The only plausible upgrade is Ram 2009 (vowel acoustics, unpublished JNU thesis), which is unlikely to change the classification. No recode or re-read needed
